item.title: Lie Hermitian manifolds with constant mixed curvature
item.description: arXiv:2611.08515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Tang's conjecture on compact Hermitian manifolds. We prove that this conjecture holds for two special classes of unimodular Lie groups: their associated Lie algebras are either almost abelian, or contain a J-invariant abelian ideal of codimension two.
item.dc:creator: Yuqin Guo, Dongmei Zhang

item.title: Rigidity, Regularity and Compactness of Special Lagrangian Submanifolds under Simons Stability
item.description: arXiv:2611.08562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that, for suitable values of $\delta$, every complete connected $\delta$-Simons stable special Lagrangian immersion in ${\mathbb C}^n$, $n\ge3$, is flat. We also prove that a $\delta$-Simons stable special Lagrangian cone $C\subset{\mathbb C}^n$ with $C\cap{\mathbb S}^{2n-1}$ smooth and compact is a finite union of planes if $\delta>(n-2)^2/(4n)$, and that this coefficient is optimal. At equality, we characterize the $\delta$-Simons stable cones. We further establish regularity and compactness for sequences of proper $\delta$-Simons stable special Lagrangian immersions when $n\ge3$ and $\delta>(n-2)/(n+1)$, under suitable restrictions on the initial singular sets, assuming integral current extensions $T_j$ with $\partial T_j=0$ and uniformly bounded mass on compact subsets. In dimension three, we allow initial singular sets $S_j$ satisfying $\mathcal H^1(S_j)=0$. For suitable values of $\delta$, we also prove properness, Euclidean volume growth, and finite total curvature for complete connected immersions of finite $\delta$-index.
item.dc:creator: Caiyan Li

item.title: The Gibbons--Penrose inequality in Minkowski spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.08609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Gibbons--Penrose inequality for smooth closed spacelike codimension-two submanifolds of Minkowski spacetime whose past null second fundamental form is non-negative. The proof is motivated by the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci technique.
item.dc:creator: Jingbo Wan, Yipeng Wang

item.title: Projective flatness of cylindrically symmetric Finsler metrics
item.description: arXiv:2611.08747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study cylindrically symmetric projectively flat Finsler metrics \(F=|\bar y|\phi(x^0,r,s,z)\). We reformulate the conditions for projective flatness and strong convexity in terms of \(\Omega=\phi-s\phi_s-z\phi_z\), isolating the compatibility condition missing in earlier work. Using the method of characteristics, we give an integral formula for all smooth local solutions near points with \(r>0\) and \(s=z=0\). These solutions are determined by a characteristic potential up to the addition of an invariant exact one-form. In the reversible case, the equation for the potential reduces to a \((2+1)\)-dimensional wave equation on a half-space. We illustrate the reconstruction with a polynomial potential and compute the potentials of a known family of spherically symmetric metrics and their linear pullbacks. The convexity conditions also admit decreasing profiles and recover the spherical Beltrami metric as a particular case. Finally, suitable positive sums of linear pullbacks yield smooth reversible projectively flat Finsler metrics on \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) whose tangent norm at the origin is non-Riemannian. Consequently, these metrics are not linear pullbacks of spherically symmetric metrics
item.dc:creator: Newton Sol\'orzano, V\'ictor Le\'on, Dik Lujerio

item.title: A new characterization of the round sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.08751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We provide an elementary proof of Hersch's inequality and Cheng's theorem, both characterizing the sphere. We revisit these classical results in connection with the geodesic monotonicity of heat kernels on two-dimensional spheres, which provides a third characterization.
item.dc:creator: Almut Burchard, \'Angel D. Mart\'inez

item.title: Left-Invariant Kernels of the Hodge-de Rham Operator on Three-Dimensional Lorentzian Lie Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.08815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the kernel of the Hodge--de Rham operator on left-invariant differential forms for the seven customary families of three-dimensional Lorentzian metric Lie algebras. Every parameter stratum is treated, including zero structure constants, singular bracket matrices, and null modular directions. If $\theta(X)=\mathrm{tr}\,\mathrm{ad}_X$ is the modular character, the full kernel is the direct sum of constants, the space $K=\mathrm{Ann}([\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{g}])\cap\theta^\perp$, its Hodge dual, and the volume forms. We give explicit real bases in all seven families and compute the exterior differential and geometric codifferential on every basis form. The non-unimodular calculation remains valid without the customary extra normalization conditions, and hence also covers metric representatives omitted by those conditions. The resulting dimensions are $2,4,6$, or $8$; the two middle-degree dimensions agree. Explicit examples distinguish the kernel of the first-order operator from the kernel of its square. All assertions concern smooth left-invariant forms, with no square-integrability condition.
item.dc:creator: Fanqi Lin

item.title: Differentiation of tepui groupoids and the holonomy groupoid of singular foliations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tepui groupoids are a generalization of Lie groupoids which allow the arrow space to be singular, as is the case for holonomy groupoids of singular foliations. We construct a Lie differentiation functor for a large class of tepui groupoids. When restricted to effective and source-connected tepui groupoids, this differentiation recovers the correspondence between holonomy groupoids and their underlying singular foliations.
item.dc:creator: Alfonso Garmendia, David Miyamoto, Leonid Ryvkin

item.title: An improved isodiametric inequality for convex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alexandrov conjectured that every closed convex surface of area $A$ and intrinsic diameter $D$ satisfies $A/D^2\leq\pi/2$. Using an averaging argument over the curvature measure, we prove that every closed convex surface satisfies $A/D^2\leq2\pi/3$, improving the best previously known bound.
item.dc:creator: Mat\v{e}j Stehl\'ik

item.title: A Poincare-Einstein Liouville Theorem and the Yamabe Invariant of Lens Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schoen conjectured that the Yamabe invariant of every lens space is achieved by the round metric. A proof of this conjecture is presented for all lens spaces, together with rigidity: equality is only achieved for the round class. The key step is to show that every $\mathbb Z_p$-invariant Yamabe-positive conformal class on $S^3$ admits a $\mathbb Z_p$-equivariant Poincar\'e-Einstein filling. The distance function from a fixed point of the filling then gives an invariant test function with Yamabe quotient at most $\sigma(S^3)$, which descends to the lens space. The proof of the main theorem was generated by AI (ChatGPT Astra, September 2026); this is mainly a learning note of the AI generated proof.
item.dc:creator: Liam Mazurowski, Tongrui Wang, Xuan Yao, Xin Zhou

item.title: A splitting theorem for Einstein manifolds with symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2611.09257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every negative-Einstein manifold with cocompact symmetries splits isometrically as a Riemannian product $H \times K$ with $H$ homogeneous and $K$ compact. This confirms a conjecture due to B\"ohm and Lafuente. As a consequence, we obtain a new proof of the 1975 Alekseevskii conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Martinez Wagner

item.title: Higher Holonomy for Higher Lie Algebroid Connections on Graded Vector Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.09300v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of a Riemann--Hilbert $A_\infty$-functor from the curved dg-category of $\mathscr{A}$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $\mathscr{A}$ is a higher Lie algebroid, to the curved dg-category of $\Pi_\infty(\mathscr{A})$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $\Pi_\infty(\mathscr{A})$ is the homotopy groupoid of $\mathscr{A}$. When restricted to the sub dg-categories of flat objects, it induces an $A_\infty$-functor from the dg-category of representations up to homotopy of $\mathscr{A}$ to the dg-category of representations up to homotopy of $\Pi_\infty(\mathscr{A})$, which recovers the one from arXiv:1011.4693 and arXiv:0908.2843 when $\mathscr{A}$ is a Lie algebroid. The key ingredient for defining such functors is a non-abelian Stokes's theorem for endomorphism-valued differential forms. Furthermore, for a graded vector bundle $E$, we introduce the notion of its higher general linear groupoid in such a way that $G$-connections on $E$, for a higher Lie groupoid $G$, become smooth functors from $G$ to the higher general linear groupoid of $E$. We combine this with the Riemann--Hilbert functor to define higher parallel transport functors for $\mathscr{A}$-connections. Finally, we use these functors to define the higher holonomy groups of $\mathscr{A}$-connections and endow them with the structure of augmented simplicial Lie groups.
item.dc:creator: Sven Holtrop, Jaime Pedregal

item.title: Natural potentials for TT tensors, divergence-free symmetric tensors and linearised relativistic initial data
item.description: arXiv:2611.09303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $N$ be a natural tensor which vanishes at a metric $g\_0$. By diffeomorphism invariance, $DN(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in TT tensors if moreover $DN(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. Such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. On Einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised Bach tensor gives the operator $P$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on TT tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on Bach-flat, conformally flat and Ricci-parallel metrics. Replacing the diffeomorphisms of $M$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a Fredholm property, for the linearised Einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Erwann Delay (LMA, AU)

item.title: Deformation of Associative Submanifolds joining Minimal Surfaces in Hyperbolic Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.09689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Donaldson and Thomas proposed a Floer-type theory on a Calabi-Yau threefold $M$, generated by the complex curves, and whose boundary operator is given by counting appropriate associative submanifolds in $M\times \mathbb{R}$. We consider a similar setting, in which the Calabi-Yau manifold is replaced by the twistor space $Z$ of an oriented hyperbolic 4-manifold $X$ and the $J$-holomorphic curves in $Z$ project to minimal surfaces in $X$. We give a formula for the virtual dimension of (a subset of) the moduli space of associatives asymptotic to a pair of $J$-holomorphic curves in $Z$, proving it equals the difference of the Morse indices of the corresponding minimal surfaces in $X$.
item.dc:creator: Maxime Weytens

item.title: A generalization of the Gauss Lemma
item.description: arXiv:2611.09784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a generalization of the Gauss Lemma for normal exponential maps and a covering criterion as a consequence.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Scoffone

item.title: Neutral Ricci spectra of homogeneous Riemannian four-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.09824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that every quadruple of real numbers with two positive and two negative entries is the Ricci spectrum of some left-invariant Riemannian metric on a Lie group of dimension four. Consequently, for eight out of the fifteen possible Ricci signatures of four-dimensional homogeneous Riemannian manifolds, one can determine precisely which spectra in each given signature actually occur. We also describe the Ricci spectra realized by left-invariant metrics on a certain class of 2-step solvable Lie groups of all dimensions $n>2$.
item.dc:creator: Andrzej Derdzinski, JeongHyeong Park

item.title: Radial reductions of variable exponent Laplacian equations on warped products with compact symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2611.09826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study nonlinear elliptic equations of variable exponent type, \[ -\Delta_{q(x)}u+|u|^{q(x)-2}u=f(x,u), \] on non-compact Riemannian manifolds with symmetry. We consider complete warped products \[ M=\mathcal R\times_\phi Y,\qquad g_\phi=dr^2\oplus\phi(r)^2g_Y, \] where $\mathcal R$ is a non-compact interval, possibly with boundary, and $Y$ is a compact homogeneous manifold. We establish sufficient conditions on the warping function ensuring a Ricci lower bound, a uniform non-collapsing volume condition, and the orbit-growth hypothesis of the abstract existence theorem proved in \cite{JFA}. We also obtain comparison bounds for the admissible warping functions. We analyze the corresponding radial equations for the admissible exponential and linear models $\phi(r)=e^{ar}$ and $\phi(r)=ar$, with $r\geq r_0>0$. For a constant diffusion exponent $q=k$, we consider explicit decaying profiles $u=\phi^{-\sigma}$, which belong to $L_1^k(M)$ provided $\sigma k>\dim Y$ in the exponential case and $\sigma k>\dim Y+1$ in the linear case. Under additional explicit parameter restrictions, these profiles solve a resonant equation with a positive bounded coefficient, a construction distinct from the superlinear regime of the abstract existence theorem. Finally, we establish logarithmic reductions for constant and variable radial exponents, and justify the passage from radial identities to weak formulations against arbitrary compactly supported interior test functions.
item.dc:creator: Jose Luis Diaz Palencia, Daniel J. Pons, Enrique G. Reyes

item.title: Non-conical classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated singularity
item.description: arXiv:2611.08670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Several examples of one-homogeneous classical solutions to the one-phase free boundary problem with an isolated free boundary singularity are known. Adapting the approach of Caffarelli, Hardt, and Simon for minimal surfaces, we construct non-conical classical solutions with an isolated free boundary singularity by perturbing a one-homogeneous solution $U$. Moreover, if $U$ is strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate), then any solution sufficiently close to $U$ is also strictly stable (respectively, non-degenerate).
item.dc:creator: Minyoung Jeong

item.title: Regularity of Weak Solutions near Singular Minimizing Cones for the One-Phase Free Boundary Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.08688v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Alt and Caffarelli proved an Allard-type $\epsilon$-regularity theorem near the flat one-homogeneous minimizer of the one-phase free boundary problem. A natural follow-up question is whether an analogous regularity result holds near singular minimizing cones. In this paper, we prove such an $\epsilon$-regularity theorem near a strongly integrable one-phase minimizing cone with an isolated singularity. More precisely, we show that, after a suitable translation and rotation, the free boundary of any non-degenerate weak solution sufficiently close to the cone is graphical over the free boundary of a leaf of the De Silva--Jerison--Shahgholian foliation. This result is analogous to recent $\epsilon$-regularity theorems in minimal surface theory by Edelen and by Edelen--Spolaor; our proof adapts the strategy of Edelen to the one-phase setting.
item.dc:creator: Minyoung Jeong

item.title: Multi-monopoles and monodromy around the wobbly divisor
item.description: arXiv:2611.08760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The multi-monopole equations are a generalisation of the Seiberg--Witten equations where the spinor is coupled to an auxiliary vector bundle. The signed count of multi-monopoles on a 3-manifold can vary according to a new type of wall-crossing phenomenon. For products $S^1\times C$, where $C$ is a closed Riemann surface, we relate the wall and chamber structure to loops in the complement of the wobbly divisor of $C$. Such a loop induces a monodromy map on the multi-vortex moduli space, and the count of its fixed points is expected to agree with the count of multi-monopoles on $S^1\times C$ in the given chamber. By studying singularities of framed multi-vortex moduli spaces, we are able to understand these monodromy maps for various loops. Counting fixed points suggests that product 3-manifolds display incredibly rich wall-crossing behaviour.
item.dc:creator: Brad Wilson

item.title: Finite-Scale Folding and Maximal Asymptotic Variance
item.description: arXiv:2611.09697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm

item.title: Smooth atlas stratified spaces, K-Homology Orientations, and Gysin maps, Part 1
item.description: arXiv:2505.14952v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce smooth atlas stratified spaces. We show that this class is closed under cartesian products; consequently, it is possible to define fiber bundles of smooth atlas stratified spaces. We describe the resolution of such a space to a manifold with fibered corners and use this result in order to prove that the class of smooth atlas stratified spaces coincides with that of Thom-Mather stratified spaces. We then consider Witt pseudomanifolds (such as singular complex algebraic varieties) where it is well-known that a bordism invariant signature is available and equal to the Fredholm index of a realization of the signature operator. To each oriented fiber bundle of stratified spaces, with Witt fibers, we assign a class in bivariant KK-theory (with 2 inverted). Kasparov multiplication by this element defines a Gysin map in analytic K-homology and one of our main results is that this Gysin map preserves the analytic signature class of Witt spaces. We prove in fact a more general result: functoriality for fiber bundles in the sense that if one fiber bundle is the composition of two others then the KK-class of the former is the Kasparov product of the classes of the latter. We also discuss this result for other Dirac-type operators satisfying an analytic Witt condition, for example the spin-Dirac operator on a fibration of psc-Witt spin pseudomanifolds. We next define the analytic Gysin map associated to an oriented normally non-singular inclusion of Witt spaces and prove that it also preserves the signature class. Finally, we relate the analytic signature class of a Witt space with the topological Siegel-Sullivan orientation. Specifically we show that if one applies the inverse of the second Adams operation to the Sullivan orientation and complexifies then one obtains our analytic signature class under the natural identification between analytic and topological K-homology.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Albin, Markus Banagl, Paolo Piazza

item.title: Transformation theorem and monotonicity of the numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls
item.description: arXiv:2607.06277v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In \cite{HH}, H. Huang-X.Huang introduced the generalized Reifenberg condition which describes the non-increasing property of numbers of almost Euclidean factors of geodesic balls and gave a transformation theorem under this condition. In this note, we study how almost Euclidean factors of concentric geodesic balls interact with harmonic splitting maps under a lower Ricci curvature bound and prove a dimension gap for harmonic functions of almost linear growth and then derive a transformation theorem under a non-decreasing property compared with the non-increasing property above. We also construct complete manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose balls are uniformly almost $1$-Euclidean at every scale, but for which no single harmonic function can be transformed into a splitting function at all smaller scales which give a negative answer to the existence question for all-scale splitting functions in \cite{HH}.
item.dc:creator: Lina Chen

item.title: Topological Rigidity of Contractible 3-Manifolds and Handlebody Interiors under Nonnegative Scalar Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2607.25015v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a contractible $3$-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature is diffeomorphic to $\R^3$. We also prove that, if the interior of a compact handlebody of genus $\gamma$ admits such a metric, then $\gamma\leq1$. This answers two open questions posed by Wang and Gromov, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Jiangcheng You, Heng Zhang

item.title: Schwarzian Residue of the Samuelson Obstruction in Tangent Lagrangian 2-Webs
item.description:
arXiv:2608.09825v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Samuelson condition, a classical area-ratio condition for planar Lagrangian $2$-webs, is equivalent in local web coordinates $(u,v)$ to $\partial_u\partial_v\log|J_F(u,v)|=0$, where $F$ is the inverse web-coordinate map and $J_F$ is its Jacobian. For the tangent-line family $L_t: y=tx+h(t)$, with $h$ smooth on an open interval, let $\Psi(u,v)$, for $u
eq v$, be the intersection map of $L_u$ and $L_v$, write $J_{\Psi}$ for its Jacobian, and set $S_h(u,v) := \partial_u\partial_v\log|J_{\Psi}(u,v)|$ where $J_{\Psi}(u,v)
eq0$. Near each diagonal point $(t_0,t_0)$ with $h''(t_0)
eq0$, the obstruction admits the decomposition $S_h(u,v) =  rac{1}{(v-u)^2} + R_h(u,v)$, where $R_h$ extends smoothly across the diagonal near $(t_0,t_0)$. The universal pole yields $S_h(u,v)>0$ off the diagonal in a sufficiently small neighborhood of $(t_0,t_0)$, so the tangent web does not satisfy the Samuelson condition there. We call $R_h(t,t)$ the Schwarzian residue and show that $R_h(t,t) =  rac{1}{2}\{\sigma,t\} = -\kappa_{\mathrm{aff}}(\sigma) \left( rac{d\sigma}{dt}ight)^2$. Here $\sigma$ is the equi-affine arclength parameter of the envelope $\gamma(t)=(-h'(t),h(t)-t h'(t))$, and $\{\sigma,t\}$ denotes the Schwarzian derivative of $\sigma$ with respect to $t$. The equi-affine curvature $\kappa_{\mathrm{aff}}$ is defined by $\gamma_{\sigma\sigma\sigma}+\kappa_{\mathrm{aff}}\gamma_\sigma=0$. We also derive the transformation law of the residue under reparametrization of the tangent-line family.
item.dc:creator: Yasuhiro Kurokawa

item.title: Projective Rigidity of $U(k)$-Radial Ricci-Flat K\"ahler Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2609.21950v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study K\"ahler immersions of Ricci-flat metrics into finite- or infinite-dimensional complex projective space. Let $L^{\otimes k}\simeq K_X$ over a real-analytic K\"ahler manifold $X$. Let $\phi$ be a base potential and $s$ the canonical squared fibre norm on $L^{\oplus k}$. Consider Ricci-flat potentials $\phi+h(s)$ near the zero section, with $h$ independent of the base point. We prove that local projective inducibility forces the base to be Ricci-flat and the metric to split locally as $X\times\mathbb C^k$. In that case projective inducibility is equivalent to that of the base. The proof combines Calabi's criterion, positivity of the homogeneous fibre-degree blocks, and the singularities of the radial profile. A related obstruction along holomorphic curves excludes every positive multiple of the Taub--NUT metric and Calabi's hyperk\"ahler metrics on $T^{*1,0}\mathbb{CP}^n$. Applications also include the resolved conifold, canonical-bundle metrics in non-Einstein classes, and Cifarelli's rank-two Type-2 metric.
item.dc:creator: Shaosai Huang

item.title: Total Mean Curvature Gaps for Scalar-Flat Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24653v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a complete connected scalar-flat Euclidean hypersurface of dimension $n\geq3$ is an affine hyperplane if its normalized mean curvature has sufficiently small $L^n$ norm. We also compute the total mean curvature energy of a classical rotational scalar-flat family to show that finiteness cannot replace smallness in dimensions $n\geq3$.
item.dc:creator: Jiuru Zhou

item.title: The first gap for minimal submanifolds in spheres
item.description: arXiv:2611.08126v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f:M^n\to\Sn^{n+q}(1)$ be a minimal immersion of a closed connected manifold with $n\ge3$ and $q\ge2$, and let $S$ be the squared length of its second fundamental form. We prove an integral inequality that gives $\max_M S\ge n$ if the immersion is not totally geodesic. If $n\ne4$ or $q=2$, equality $\max_M S=n$ holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface; if $n=4$ and $q\ge3$, equality holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface or the standard minimal embedding of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ in $\Sn^7(1)$. Both classifications are understood up to an ambient isometry, a totally geodesic inclusion, and a finite covering. We construct the integral inequalities using polynomial weights and divergence identities. The required algebraic estimates are proved by sums of squared tensor norms.
item.dc:creator: Jianquan Ge, Kai Jia, Fagui Li

item.title: Biholomorphic rigidity and symmetry breaking for domains with Bergman metric of constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.13831v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Based on earlier work by Wiegerinck and Huang-Li, Hayashida-Kamimoto constructed unbounded non-smooth Reinhardt domains in \({\mathbb C}^n\), \(n\geq 3\), whose Bergman spaces are finite-dimensional and whose Bergman metrics have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). In this note, we prove a Sandwich Principle for the Hayashida-Kamimoto domains that allows us to construct, inside every prescribed sandwich, uncountably many pairwise biholomorphically inequivalent smooth non-Reinhardt domains whose Bergman metrics also have constant positive holomorphic sectional curvature \(2\). We also classify biholomorphisms between domains sandwiched by the domains of Hayashida-Kamimoto with the help of an affine rigidity theorem in the spirit of Cartan rigidity, which should be of independent interest. For explicit angular perturbation families, we determine the full automorphism group and obtain, in particular, an abundance of examples with trivial automorphism group.
item.dc:creator: Gordon Heier, Ravi Mudaliar, Haotian Zuo

item.title: No Connectedness Lemma for Alexandrov spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.37476v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Since its introduction in 2003, Wilking's Connectedness Lemma has become a powerful tool in the study of manifolds with positive sectional curvature. In recent work of the authors, this has been extended to orbifolds. The purpose of this note is to exhibit counterexamples in the class of Alexandrov spaces for the Connectedness Lemma in both its ordinary and dual formulation. This answers a 2007 question of Wilking.
item.dc:creator: Jan Nienhaus, Dennis Wulle
